en.title: Minimum Operations to Unify Prices for Independent Queries
en.description:
Each operation adds 1 to or subtracts 1 from one element. For each query value, find the minimum number of operations to turn all elements into that value. Queries are independent; the original array is restored before the next query.

The standard input/output format was compiled by this site; added numeric bounds and the encoding for no-solution cases are explicitly marked and do not claim to be the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n q, the second line contains the array, and the third line contains q queries. The source has no numeric bounds; on this site 1≤n,q≤100000, and the array values and queries are integers in −10^9..10^9.
en.output: Output q lines of integers in query order.
en.explanation: The examples give 14 and 10; 20; and 0, 3, 0 respectively.
hints: After sorting, compute prefix sums, use binary search to separate the numbers less than the target from those not less than it, and compute the increases and decreases separately.
